answer.rationale: Incumbent will not reopen price and the primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so renew, negotiate, or defer cannot meet the 18% spend cut without a supply hole. The low-cost quote meets the mandate on its own. memory_c2 is the load-bearing precedent (prior primary move to this vendor cut cost, onboarding described as quick, invoicing accurate) and I am verifying it before treating that onboarding as compatible with a 14-day window. memory_c1 still argues renew is the lower operational-risk path. Assembly is at 94% with no buffer, so a full primary switch can starve the line even if unit price falls; last year’s switch does not speak to this utilization or buffer, so delivery/TCO upside is uncertain.
